properties.trigger: any competition tagged ice_hockey: games, box scores, goalie numbers, lines and pairings, standings with the loser point, playoff series, the draft, trades, waivers, affiliate assignments, reserve lists, beer-league nights, international tournaments, fantasy ice hockey slots and categories
properties.scope: competition, season, team, person, event, stat_line

data.short_description: Ice hockey at every level, from a 32-team national pro league and international tournaments to junior, college and beer league: positions and lines, periods and overtime formats, the shootout and the loser point, the full skater and goalie stat key set with derived rates, standings with regulation-wins tiebreakers, the 16-team divisional playoff bracket as series parent events, roster designations without reasons, officials, and the sport-specific half of fantasy ice hockey.

lore.title: Overview
lore.content:
Sport: ice hockey, at every level: a national professional league, a women's professional league, a continental pro league, the world championship and the winter games tournament, junior, college and university, minor hockey, and adult recreational (beer league). Code ice_hockey. Always say "ice hockey" in prose; the code is the tag.
A match is a game. Three 20-minute periods (shorter at some rec and youth levels: 3 x 15 or 3 x 12 running time), with intermissions after the first and second. The single score number is goals: home_score/away_score are the final goals including the one goal credited to a shootout winner. score_display carries the extra: "3-2 OT", "3-2 SO", "3-2 2OT" (playoff overtime periods are numbered), "5-0 (forfeit)".
Overtime: regular season at the top level is one 5-minute 3-on-3 sudden-death period, then a shootout (best of three, then sudden death by round). Playoff and tournament knockout games play full 20-minute 5-on-5 sudden-death periods with no shootout, so they never tie. International group games play 5-minute 3-on-3 OT then a shootout; the gold-medal game plays a 20-minute OT. Rec leagues often play no overtime and a tie stands, or a 3-minute 3-on-3 OT, or go straight to a shootout; set the house rule in a House rules chunk on the competition.
Results: home_win, away_win, tie. Never draw (the sport says tie). tie only where the league allows ties (rec, some youth, historical pro seasons). no_result for an abandoned game that is neither resumed nor replayed. decided_by: regulation, overtime, shootout, forfeit, run_rule. A shootout win is a win in the record with decided_by shootout; the loser gets the loser point (see Standings). Individual shootout goals never count as goals or points for the shooter and the deciding goal is not a game-winning goal.
Default competition: level pro (or recreational, international, college, youth), format league_playoffs for a pro league, league for a rec league without playoffs, group_knockout for an international tournament, series for a stand-alone best-of series. scoring_system: 2-1-0 for the pro loser-point system (W 2, OTL/SOL 1, L 0), 3-2-1-0 for international (regulation win 3, OT/SO win 2, OT/SO loss 1, regulation loss 0), 2-1-0 with ties for rec (W 2, T 1, L 0). Season label is the split year "2026-27"; season tag <competition fragment>-2026-27. Every entity in this sport carries the tag ice_hockey.
Home and away: the designated home team is home even at a neutral-site showcase or outdoor game; set HELD_AT to the actual arena. A tournament game on neutral ice is neutral_site true with neutral_first for the team listed first by the organiser.
Tags the pack owns on its entities: ice_hockey, match, stats, series, shootout, three-stars, lines, roster-designation, book-kept, no-book, affiliate, fantasy-hockey.

lore.title: Positions
lore.content:
Position codes on PLAYS_FOR.position (and PLAYED_IN.position when it differs on the night):
C: centre. Takes faceoffs; the middle forward.
LW: left wing.
RW: right wing.
F: forward, when the league or the owner does not split wings from centres (rec leagues, many box scores, fantasy utility). Prefer C/LW/RW when known.
D: defence (defenceman, defender). Pairs, not lines.
G: goaltender (goalie).
secondary_positions: a wing who also takes draws gets ["C"]; a defender who plays forward gets ["F"]. A skater is anyone who is not a G; the pack uses "skater" for the stat split, never as a position.
Handedness on person: shoots_left, shoots_right for skaters; catches_left, catches_right for goalies (the glove hand). Only for adult professionals and only when the owner gives it.
Depth: depth_order on PLAYS_FOR is the line for forwards (1-4), the pair for defence (1-3) and 1 (starter) or 2 (backup) for goalies; a healthy scratch is role bench with depth_order empty. Who skates with whom, the power-play and penalty-kill units and the extra-attacker group are a lore chunk on the team titled "Lines", one dated block per game or per change, written as the coach would read it: "Line 1: Lee - Kim - Park. Pair 1: Diaz - Novak. PP1: Lee, Kim, Park, Diaz, Novak. PK1: Kim, Park, Diaz, Novak. G: Okafor (Lam)."
Leadership: role captain for the C, role vice_captain for each A (two or three alternates is normal; some teams rotate the A, note it in Lines). A rec team's organiser who also plays gets STAFF_OF role captain_organiser as well.

lore.title: Stages and rounds
lore.content:
stage values on events and seasons:
preseason: exhibition games before the season; never count in standings or season stats unless the owner says so (tag preseason).
regular_season: the league schedule.
playoffs is the season stage; playoff games carry the round stage: round_1 (first round, 16 teams at the top level), round_2 (second round), conference_final, final (the championship series). Leagues with named rounds (quarterfinal, semifinal, final) use those. play_in for a qualifying round.
group_stage, quarterfinal, semifinal, bronze_medal, final: international tournaments and cups. relegation_round for the tournament's relegation games.
all_star: all-star or skills events, never counted.
exhibition: a one-off friendly, a rec-league scrimmage, an alumni game.
round: for regular_season the owner's unit ("Game 23" for a team's game number, "Week 9" for a rec league or a fantasy week, or empty); for a series child event "Game N"; for a group stage "Matchday 3". Playoff games are children of a series parent event: the parent is event_type match, stage round_1 (or whichever), status in_progress until the series ends, score_display the series count "3-1", result the series outcome, and the child games are PART_OF it with round "Game N". The parent carries date_* of Game 1 and end_date of the clincher. A single-game knockout (international quarterfinal, a cup round) needs no parent.
decided_by: regulation (default when the game ended after three periods), overtime (any OT goal, regular season or playoff), shootout (regular season and international group games only), forfeit, run_rule (rec and youth leagues that end or stop the clock at a goal margin; the margin goes in House rules).
A playoff game can never be decided by shootout; if the owner says so, ask whether it was a tournament group game.

lore.title: Stat keys
lore.content:
Keys for the stats object. All lowercase snake_case, all numbers; null for not recorded. Match-scope lines hold one game; season and career lines hold sums. Rate stats are derived unless marked stored. Derived rates are computed only over lines whose components are non-null, and the AI says how many games that covers.
Skater keys (any non-goalie):
gp: games played (1 on a match line when they dressed and played).
g: goals.
a: assists (primary and secondary together).
a1: primary assists, when tracked.
a2: secondary assists, when tracked.
pts: points. Stored (so leaders can be filtered on it) and must equal g + a; the AI checks and flags a mismatch.
plus_minus: plus/minus, even-strength and shorthanded goals for minus against while on the ice; may be negative.
pim: penalty minutes, as the scoresheet totals them (minor 2, double minor 4, major 5, misconduct 10, game misconduct 10, match penalty 10). A stat, not a disciplinary record.
shots: shots on goal.
missed_shots: shot attempts that missed the net, when tracked.
blocked_shot_attempts: own attempts blocked by an opponent, when tracked.
hits: hits credited.
blocks: opponents' shots blocked.
takeaways: takeaways.
giveaways: giveaways.
toi_seconds: time on ice in seconds (18:32 is stored as 1112). Never store mm:ss text. Because the pack has this key, PLAYED_IN.minutes stays empty in ice hockey.
pp_toi_seconds: power-play time on ice in seconds.
pk_toi_seconds: penalty-kill (shorthanded) time on ice in seconds.
shifts: number of shifts.
ppg: power-play goals.
ppa: power-play assists.
ppp: power-play points, stored, must equal ppg + ppa.
shg: shorthanded goals.
sha: shorthanded assists.
shp: shorthanded points, stored, must equal shg + sha.
evg: even-strength goals.
eva: even-strength assists.
gwg: game-winning goals (the goal that put the winner one ahead of the loser's final total; never a shootout goal).
otg: overtime goals.
eng: empty-net goals.
fow: faceoffs won.
fol: faceoffs lost.
so_attempts: shootout attempts taken.
so_goals: shootout goals scored (never added to g or pts).
so_gdg: shootout game-deciding goals.
penalties_drawn: penalties drawn, when tracked.
penalties_taken: penalties taken (count, not minutes), when tracked.
Derived skater rates: shooting_pct = g / shots. fo_pct = fow / (fow + fol). pts_per_gp = pts / gp. toi_per_gp = toi_seconds / gp (present as mm:ss). pim_per_gp = pim / gp. a1_share = a1 / a when both tracked.
Goalie keys:
gp: games played (any appearance).
gs: games started.
w: wins (1 on the match line for the goalie of record in a win, including shootout wins).
l: losses in regulation (goalie of record).
otl: overtime and shootout losses (goalie of record). In a league with ties use t instead.
t: ties (rec and historical).
ga: goals against, charged to this goalie; empty-net goals against are never charged to a goalie.
sa: shots against faced.
sv: saves. Stored; must equal sa - ga.
so: shutouts (1 when the goalie played the whole game and allowed no goal; a shared shutout counts for neither).
toi_seconds: time on ice in seconds.
pim: goalie penalty minutes.
g: goalie goals (rare; credited like a skater).
a: goalie assists.
so_shots_faced: shootout attempts faced.
so_saves: shootout saves.
so_ga: shootout goals allowed.
qs: quality starts, when the owner tracks them (started and sv_pct at or above the league average for the game).
rbs: really bad starts (sv_pct under .850), when tracked.
Derived goalie rates: sv_pct = sv / sa (present to three decimals, ".917"). gaa = ga * 3600 / toi_seconds (goals against per 60 minutes; always per 60 even where periods are shorter). gsaa (goals saved above average) only when the owner supplies the league average sv_pct: (league_sv_pct * sa) - ga. qs_pct = qs / gs.

Team keys, match scope (one line per team per game) and season scope (sums):
goals_for: goals scored (match: equals this side's score on the event; season: sum). Alias gf in prose.
goals_against: goals allowed. Alias ga in prose; on a team line ga means goals against.
goals_p1, goals_p2, goals_p3, goals_ot: goals by period on the team line. The same line score may also go in the event's periods array when the owner wants it on the game: one element per period with number (1, 2, 3, 4 for OT), home and away goals; the shootout is not a period. goals_so: shootout goals scored (not in goals_for).
shots_for: shots on goal for. shots_against: shots on goal against.
pp_opportunities: power-play chances. pp_goals: power-play goals scored.
pk_times_shorthanded: times shorthanded. pk_goals_allowed: power-play goals allowed.
sh_goals_for: shorthanded goals scored. sh_goals_against: shorthanded goals allowed.
en_goals_for: empty-net goals scored. en_goals_against: empty-net goals allowed (charged to the team, not a goalie).
pim: team penalty minutes. penalties: count of penalties.
hits, blocks, giveaways, takeaways: team totals.
fow, fol: team faceoffs won and lost.
Derived team rates: pp_pct = pp_goals / pp_opportunities. pk_pct = 1 - pk_goals_allowed / pk_times_shorthanded. fo_pct = fow / (fow + fol). shooting_pct = goals_for / shots_for. save_pct_team = 1 - goals_against / shots_against (exclude en_goals_against if tracked). pdo = shooting_pct + save_pct_team.
Standings keys live on the team season line (see Standings): gp, w, l, otl, t, pts, rw, otw, sow, row, gf, ga, home_w, home_l, home_otl, away_w, away_l, away_otl, div_w, div_l, div_otl, conf_w, conf_l, conf_otl, so_w, so_l, streak_len (signed: +4 is W4, -2 is L2, ot losses count as losses for the streak), last10_w, last10_l, last10_otl, pts_pct (derived, see Standings).
Fantasy keys on a real player's round-scope or match-scope line RECORDED_IN the fantasy matchup: fantasy_points, projected_points (universal), plus any of the keys above the platform scores on (g a pts ppp shg sog hits blocks for skaters; w ga sa sv so for goalies). sog is an accepted alias key only inside fantasy lines because platforms use it; on real lines the key is shots.
Scope rules: match lines are one game; round lines (scope round) are a fantasy week or a tournament's matchday; season lines sum match lines with games_played set; career lines sum seasons. Every line carries completeness: full when every key the pack lists for that scope was recorded, partial when some are null, unknown for typed-in totals; nulls are skipped when summing and a season line built from any partial line is partial. When a player changes teams mid-season, keep one season line per team (for_team set) plus a combined one if the owner wants it, and say which is which.

lore.title: Standings
lore.content:
Team season line keys: gp, w, l, otl, pts, rw (regulation wins), otw (overtime wins), sow (shootout wins), row (regulation plus overtime wins, stored, must equal rw + otw), gf, ga, plus the home_/away_/div_/conf_ splits and so_w/so_l listed under Team keys above. Leagues with ties: t instead of otl. International: w (regulation wins), otw (OT and SO wins together), otl (OT and SO losses together), l (regulation losses), pts.
How a game enters the line (the join rule/seasons_and_standings does when it rebuilds a derived line; a line with source owner or official is reported as is, never overwritten): read the team's COMPETED_IN result and the event's decided_by together. result win + regulation -> w, rw. win + overtime -> w, otw. win + shootout -> w, sow. loss + regulation -> l. loss + overtime or shootout -> otl (the loser point). tie -> t. win or loss + forfeit -> w with rw, or l, as the league awards it. Only stage regular_season and status completed or forfeited count; preseason, all_star, exhibition and playoff games never enter the table. gp = w + l + otl (+ t).
Points: 2-1-0 (pro default): pts = 2w + otl (+ t). 3-2-1-0 (international): pts = 3rw + 2otw + otl. 2-1-0 with ties (rec): pts = 2w + t. The competition's scoring_system says which; House rules can override (some rec leagues give 3 for any win, some give the OTL point only after a shootout).
pts_pct (derived) = pts / (2 * gp) under 2-1-0, pts / (3 * gp) under 3-2-1-0; use it to order teams whose gp differ mid-season.
Columns to show, in this order, pro: Team, GP, W, L, OTL, PTS, P%, RW, ROW, GF, GA, DIFF, HOME, AWAY, S/O, L10, STRK. Rec with ties: Team, GP, W, L, T, PTS, GF, GA, DIFF. International group: Team, GP, W, OTW, OTL, L, GF, GA, DIFF, PTS. Group the pro table by COMPETES_IN conference ("Conference A") and group (the division alone, "Division North"), or whatever the league calls them; a division game is one where both teams' group values match, a conference game one where their conference values match.
Tiebreakers, pro default, applied in order, restarting whenever a step reduces the tied group:
1. Points percentage (pts_pct), when games played differ; otherwise points.
2. Regulation wins (rw).
3. Regulation plus overtime wins (row).
4. Total wins (w), shootout wins included.
5. Points earned in head-to-head games among the tied teams (if an odd number of home games between two teams, the first home game of the team with the extra home game is excluded).
6. Goal differential (gf - ga).
7. Goals for (gf).
International group tiebreakers: 1. points in head-to-head games among the tied teams; 2. goal differential in those games; 3. goals for in those games; 4. result against the nearest best-ranked team outside the tied group; 5. seeding coming into the tournament. Rec default: points, then head-to-head, then goal differential, then goals for, then fewest pim; House rules override.
Playoff format, pro default: 16 teams, eight per conference, the top three in each division plus two wild cards per conference. Divisional bracket: the division winner with the better record plays the lower wild card, the other division winner plays the higher wild card, and the second and third place teams in each division play each other; winners meet in round_2 inside the division, then conference_final, then final. All series best-of-seven with home ice 2-2-1-1-1 to the higher seed. Seeds go on COMPETES_IN seed; a wild card's seed is noted with detail in lore ("WC1"). Say the bracket is read off the series parent events by stage and never create a bracket entity.
Always name the tiebreaker that split any tied teams and say how many games the lines cover. If the owner has not logged every game (most fans log one team), say the table is partial and give only what the record supports: usually their own team's record, division record and streak, never a fabricated league table.

lore.title: Roster rules
lore.content:
Dressed lineup: 20 per game at the top level, 18 skaters and 2 goalies (international: 20 skaters and 2 goalies may be named, 22 total). A PLAYED_IN edge per dressed player with started true for the starting goalie and the opening five skaters if the owner cares, played false for the backup goalie who did not enter and for healthy scratches who are listed. A goalie who relieved the starter gets entered_at ("2nd period 07:41"). Rec leagues dress however many show up (see Recreational).
Active roster at the top level: 23 players maximum during the season, no minimum beyond two goalies; the owner's league may differ (House rules). College and junior squads are larger; international tournament rosters are fixed once named.
Reserve lists are roster designations with no reason attached: role injured_reserve on PLAYS_FOR with roster_list naming the list (ir, ltir; non_roster for a non-roster player; active for the active roster, which may be left blank), and the move on and off is an event with event_type roster_move (INVOLVED_IN person role subject with detail "placed on IR" / "activated", team role to_team), so the dates are the events and nothing else is stored. availability on the same edge: unavailable while on a list or scratched for any reason, doubtful for a game-time decision, suspended for a league or team suspension (the league's stated length and policy wording in lore on the person), available otherwise. The body region, "upper/lower body", "day-to-day", "week-to-week" and any medical term are never stored anywhere.
Affiliate assignment (the farm team, a conditioning stint, a junior loan): the affiliate is its own team PART_OF the parent franchise and competes in its own competition. Use the loan pattern: open PLAYS_FOR on the affiliate with arrangement loan and acquired_via assignment (or conditioning_stint), the parent edge stays open with role reserve and a lore note on the person; recall ends the loan edge and restores the parent role. The assignment and the recall are each an event with event_type roster_move when the owner wants the date. Waivers: a player claimed off waivers is a signing event with acquired_via waiver_claim; a player who clears waivers and is assigned gets a lore note "cleared waivers <date>". acquired_via vocabulary for this sport: draft, trade, free_agent, waiver_claim, assignment, recall, emergency_recall, signup, tryout, unknown.
Emergency backup goalie (the building's EBUG, the beer-league ringer, a borrowed backup): PLAYS_FOR with arrangement substitute opened and closed on the game date, a PLAYED_IN edge if they dressed, and a lore note on the event. A regular pick-up goalie shared between two rec teams simply has two open amateur edges.
Captaincy: one captain (C), up to three alternates (A) as role vice_captain; goalies are not captains at the top level.
Contracts: fee as text ("$4.5M x 3", "two-way", "entry-level, 3 years", "PTO"); no-trade or no-move clauses and retained salary go in lore on the person or the trade event. The draft is seven rounds; a drafted player's rights are a lore note until they sign, when the PLAYS_FOR edge opens with acquired_via draft.
Before logging a lineup, check: two goalies dressed (ask if only one), nobody dressed whose edge is closed or whose availability is suspended (ask), no more than the league's dressed limit (warn, do not refuse).

lore.title: Officials
lore.content: OFFICIATED role values: referee (two per game at the top level, one in many rec leagues), linesman (two), video_goal_judge (the review booth), off_ice_official (goal judge, penalty timekeeper, game timekeeper; use title-style detail in lore if the owner names which), scorer (the official scorer or the beer-league scorekeeper), supervisor (the officiating supervisor at tournaments). Record officials only when the owner names them.

lore.title: Extended keys
lore.content: No extended keys yet. Add keys here as "<key>: <meaning> (added <YYYY-MM-DD>, asked by <owner>)" before using them.

lore.title: Recreational
lore.content:
Adult recreational (beer league), pick-up and most youth house leagues change the defaults:
Game shape: often 3 x 15 or 3 x 12 running time or stop-time only in the last minutes; no overtime (ties stand, result tie, 2-1-0 with ties) or a short 3-on-3 OT or a straight shootout; set in House rules on the competition. A mercy rule (clock runs or game ends at a five- or seven-goal margin) is decided_by run_rule with the margin in House rules. Game slots are late and fixed; store date_hour and date_minute because "the 10:45 game" is how people refer to it.
Rolling subs: nobody tracks shifts or minutes. Lineups are a sign-in sheet: a PLAYED_IN edge per player who showed, no started, no minutes. Short benches are normal; nine skaters and a goalie is a game.
Stats actually kept: the scoresheet has goals, assists, penalties and the goalie's goals against, sometimes shots. The default key set is g, a, pts, pim for skaters and ga, sa (if counted), w, l, t for goalies; everything else stays null. Tag a match line book-kept when the full sheet was entered and no-book when only the score is known. Season sums skip nulls (null is not zero) and the derived season line's completeness is partial whenever any match line is; rates are quoted over the games with a kept book ("shooting 18% over the 7 games with shots counted"). Do not infer plus_minus or toi_seconds.
Goalies: teams share goalies, a goalie plays for two teams in one league, the league supplies a goalie pool, or someone's buddy fills in. Each team the goalie plays for is an open amateur PLAYS_FOR edge; a one-night fill-in is arrangement substitute opened and closed on the date. A "sub goalie" ringer for the playoffs may be against the rules: the league's eligibility rule (minimum regular-season games to dress in playoffs) goes in House rules and the AI warns, never refuses.
Ringers and skaters: same substitute pattern. Eligibility for playoffs by games played is read from PLAYED_IN edges.
Levels and divisions: rec leagues sort teams into tiers (A, B, C, D or Div 1-4). The tier is the COMPETES_IN group ("Division C", "Tuesday D"); a team moving tiers between seasons gets outcome promoted or relegated.
Money, dues and jersey orders are not this world's business beyond a House rules note; never store payment details.
Youth: minor hockey (U7 through U18) and school teams carry children. Base children rules apply unchanged: is_minor true, first name and last initial, no birth date, no birth year or draft year ("a 2010"), no links, no photos, no contact details; the owner may ask for a full name only. Co-ed is the default assumption at rec level and the pack adds no gender field; a league that requires a gender mix per line puts the rule in House rules and the AI reads lines from lore.
Officials: usually one referee and one linesman, or two referees who also call lines; use referee and linesman as fits, or leave officials off.

lore.title: Professional
lore.content:
The top level adds structure the base already has homes for:
Season calendar: training camp and preseason (September), regular season of 82 games per team (October to mid-April; a team's game number is the round, "Game 23"), an all-star break or international break in February, the trade deadline (early March; season.roster_deadline holds the date; trades after it are not allowed, say so when asked to log one), the draft lottery (May), the playoffs (mid-April to June: round_1, round_2, conference_final, final), the awards show (June; WON edges to the season with the award's name in the league's words), the draft (late June, seven rounds, event draft with end_date), free agency opening (1 July; signings as events). Women's pro and continental leagues run shorter schedules on the same shape; set rounds_total to the games per team.
Playoffs: see Standings for the 16-team divisional bracket. Each series is a parent match event (stage round_1 and so on, round left empty, score_display "4-2", result and the winner's COMPETED_IN result once over), with its games as children. COMPETES_IN status eliminated for a team knocked out; the champion gets WON title Champion on the season, the runner-up Runner-up. Playoff stats are kept on separate season lines with split_label "Playoffs" (scope split) so regular-season leaders stay clean; the season line without a split is regular season only.
Salary cap and contracts: the cap is a House rules number; fee on PLAYS_FOR is the contract as text; retained salary, conditions on picks and buyouts go in lore on the trade or on the person. Do not compute cap space unless every contract is on file, and say so.
Waivers, assignments and recalls: see Roster rules. Conditioning stints (up to 14 days on the affiliate without clearing waivers) are the loan pattern with acquired_via conditioning_stint and the dates on the edge.
Reserve lists: IR (minimum seven days) and LTIR (minimum ten games and 24 days) are role injured_reserve with roster_list ir or ltir, the placement and activation as roster_move events, nothing about why. Suspensions: availability suspended with availability_until the date it ends, the league's stated number of games and the policy name in lore on the person, plus an event with event_type other if the owner wants the date.
Modern stats: shot attempts (corsi-style) and expected goals are not pack keys because they come from models that differ by site; store them under Extended keys with the source named if the owner insists, with source import and source_url. Faceoff percentage, power-play and penalty-kill percentage, PDO and per-60 rates are derived from the keys above.
Three stars: WON person -> event with title "First Star", "Second Star", "Third Star". Player of the week or month: WON to the season with the award name and detail the week.
Officials: two referees and two linesmen per game; the video review room as video_goal_judge when the owner records a coach's challenge outcome (the challenge itself goes in event lore "Key moments").
International (world championship, winter games): competition level international, format group_knockout, scoring_system 3-2-1-0; teams are team_type national; group on COMPETES_IN "Group A"; stages group_stage, quarterfinal, semifinal, bronze_medal, final; relegation_round where it applies; tie-breakers in Standings. Players on a national team keep their club edge; the national edge is a second PLAYS_FOR with arrangement representative, started and ended with the tournament.

lore.title: Fantasy
lore.content:
Fantasy ice hockey is handled by the generic rule/app_fantasy (rosters as PLAYS_FOR with arrangement fantasy_roster and slot, waivers and free agents, trades, weekly matchups as match events between fantasy teams, categories standings). This chunk supplies only what is sport-specific.
Slots (PLAYS_FOR.slot, and PLAYED_IN.slot where lineup history is kept): C, LW, RW, D, G, F (utility forward), UTIL (any skater), BN (bench), IR, IR+ (platform IR with wider eligibility). Default lineup: C C LW LW RW RW D D D G G, bench 4 (BN), IR 1; roster size 16 plus IR. Common variants: F F F instead of split wings, a UTIL, 2 IR, 3 G. The league's counts go in House rules on the fantasy competition; the lineup check reads them.
Daily lineups: most fantasy ice hockey leagues set lineups per day because real games are nightly. slot on PLAYS_FOR is today's lineup; the pack does not log a PLAYED_IN per player per day by default (a 16-player roster over a 7-day week is 112 edges). The record of a week is the matchup event's category totals on each fantasy team's round-scope stat_line RECORDED_IN the matchup. Leagues that want lineup history write slot on PLAYED_IN for the days they care about. Weekly-lineup leagues set slot once per week.
Head-to-head categories (the most common format): skater categories G, A, PPP, SOG, HIT, BLK (often also +/-, PIM, FW, SHP); goalie categories W, GAA, SV%, SO (often GA, SV). Each is won, lost or tied per week; the matchup's home_score/away_score are categories won by each side and score_display is "6-3-1" (won-lost-tied from the home side). GAA and SV% for the week are computed from the team's summed ga, sa, sv and toi_seconds across its goalies' starts, never averaged from per-game rates; a goalie minimum (two starts) is a House rule. Rotisserie uses the same categories ranked across the league over the season on the fantasy team's season line.
Points leagues, default scoring (customise in House rules): skaters g 3, a 2, ppp 1 (bonus on top of g/a), shp 1, sog 0.4, hits 0.4, blocks 0.5, gwg 1, plus_minus 0; goalies w 4, otl 1, ga -2, sv 0.2, so 3, g 3, a 2. fantasy_points on the player's round-scope line RECORDED_IN the matchup, projected_points when the platform gives one. H2H points: the matchup scores are the two totals.
Category keys on a fantasy team's weekly or season line (scope round or season, subject_kind team, RECORDED_IN the matchup or fantasy season): g, a, pts, ppp, shp, sog (alias of shots inside fantasy lines), hits, blocks, plus_minus, pim, fow, w, ga, sa, sv, so, toi_seconds, plus derived gaa and sv_pct; cats_won, cats_lost, cats_tied on the weekly line for H2H categories.
Roster moves: draft (snake, 16 rounds for a 16-slot roster, or auction), waivers (two days by default) and free agents, FAAB where used, trades with a veto window, keepers and dynasty per rule/app_fantasy. Streaming goalies and "goalie-by-team" slots are not supported by the default slot list; a league that uses them adds the slot in House rules and treats the team unit the way rule/app_fantasy says.
IR in fantasy is a slot, not a diagnosis: moving a player to IR is slot IR; the reason is never recorded and the platform's designation (out, day-to-day) maps only to availability unavailable or doubtful on the real-club edge, without the words.

lore.title: Glossary
lore.content: Skater: any player who is not a goaltender. Dressed: in the lineup for the game (20 at the top level). Healthy scratch: dressed-eligible but left out by the coach; role bench, no reason stored. Goalie of record: the goalie charged with the decision (w, l, otl). Loser point: the standings point for losing in overtime or a shootout. RW / ROW: regulation wins / regulation plus overtime wins, the standings tiebreakers. PIM: penalty minutes. Minor (2), double minor (4), major (5), misconduct (10), game misconduct (10 plus ejection), match penalty (ejection, league review). Power play (PP): skating with a numerical advantage. Penalty kill (PK, shorthanded): the disadvantage. Empty-net goal (ENG): scored when the opposing goalie has been pulled; not charged to a goalie. Faceoff (draw): the restart; fow/fol. Plus/minus: on-ice goal differential at even strength and shorthanded. Shutout (SO): a full game with no goals against by one goalie. Hat trick: three goals by one player; natural hat trick: three in a row. Game-winning goal (GWG): the goal that put the winner ahead of the loser's final total. Three stars: the game's three best players, WON edges. Line: a forward trio; pair: a defence duo; depth_order. Top six / bottom six, top four: the first two forward lines / lines three and four, the first two defence pairs. Farm team / affiliate: the minor-league team PART_OF the franchise; sent down / called up: assignment and recall. Conditioning stint: a short affiliate assignment to regain game fitness, the loan pattern. Waivers: the 24-hour window in which other teams may claim a player before assignment. IR / LTIR: reserve lists, role injured_reserve with roster_list ir or ltir, no reason stored. Entry-level contract (ELC), two-way, one-way, PTO (professional tryout): contract types, fee as text. Trade deadline: last day for trades before the playoffs. Wild card: a playoff spot for the best non-top-three teams in a conference. Home ice: the higher seed's advantage, 2-2-1-1-1 in a best-of-seven. Beer league: adult recreational; shinny / pick-up: informal games, not logged unless the owner wants them. Ringer: a non-rostered fill-in, arrangement substitute. Sub goalie: a borrowed or pool goaltender. Sign-in sheet: the rec lineup. Running time: the clock does not stop. Mercy rule: stop or end at a goal margin, decided_by run_rule. EBUG: emergency backup goalie, a building's on-call amateur. Shootout (SO): the skills tiebreak after regular-season overtime. Puck line, totals: betting terms, not pack keys.

lore.title: Season calendar
lore.content:
Pro default (northern hemisphere): training camp and preseason mid-September; regular season early October to mid-April (82 games per team; seasons labelled "2026-27"); international or all-star break early February; trade deadline early March; playoffs mid-April to late June (four best-of-seven rounds); draft lottery May; awards and draft late June; free agency opens 1 July; offseason July to September, when trades, signings and buyouts are events PART_OF the season just ended until the next season exists. Women's pro leagues run roughly November to May with fewer games on the same stage vocabulary. Continental leagues run September to late April/May.
International: the senior men's world championship in May (overlapping the pro playoffs), the women's world championship in April, the winter games tournament in February of a games year, the under-20 world championship over the turn of the year, the under-18 in April. Each is its own competition (level international, format group_knockout) with a season per edition labelled by the year and host.
College and university: October to March/April with conference tournaments then a national tournament (stage quarterfinal, semifinal, final; regionals as round_1). Junior: September to March with playoffs to May.
Recreational: three seasons a year is common (fall, winter, spring/summer); labels "Winter 2026-27", "Summer 2027"; a short playoff of one or two rounds plus a final; tiers may reshuffle between seasons.
Update season.stage and current_round when a round's games are logged; set status completed when the final (or the last regular-season game in a no-playoff league) is in.

lore.title: Forfeits and abandonments
lore.content:
Forfeit: status forfeited, decided_by forfeit, the league's awarded score in the score fields (1-0 is the common pro convention; many rec leagues award 5-0 or 3-0; House rules decide), result accordingly, why in event lore only when the reason is not medical. A forfeit counts as a regulation win and loss in the table unless House rules say otherwise. A rec team that cannot field the minimum (often five skaters and a goalie, or no goalie by ten minutes past the slot) forfeits; the pack warns when a sign-in sheet is short and asks whether the game was played.
Postponed (never started): keep the event, status postponed, update the date when rescheduled, original date in lore. Never a second event.
Suspended and resumed from the point of stoppage (glass, ice, lights, power): one event, status suspended between the two dates, date_* staying as day one and end_date the day it finished, the score at the stoppage in score_display until completed, the circumstances in lore "Conditions"; stats accumulate on the same match lines and the result enters the table on the completion date.
Abandoned and replayed from scratch: the abandoned event stays with status abandoned, result no_result, position when stopped in score_display; the replay is a new event with round "Replay" and a lore note pointing at the original. Nothing from the abandoned game counts unless the league says so (House rules). Abandoned and not replayed: status abandoned, result no_result, nothing in the table.
Cancelled (weather, no ice, season ended early): status cancelled, result no_result, never in the table. A season cut short is season status completed with ruleset_notes saying so, or cancelled if no champion was declared.
Mercy rule: decided_by run_rule, status completed, the final goals as the clock or the margin left them, the rule in House rules.
Ineligible player (a rec ringer in the playoffs, a suspended player dressed): if the league overturns the result, set status forfeited and decided_by forfeit with the awarded score, keep the played score in score_display with "(played)" and explain in lore; stats from the game stay on the lines unless the league voids them.

properties.trigger: an ice hockey game was played or is about to be: score, periods, shootout, box score, goalie numbers, sign-in sheet, three stars, series update, how are we doing

data.short_description: The game-night routine for ice hockey at any level: find or create the game, score it with the right decided_by, period and shootout detail, who dressed, the box score with the goalie of record, then update standings lines, series parents and season totals, and tell the story.

lore.title: What this covers
lore.content: The routine for one ice hockey game night at any level: a pro game the owner watched, a beer-league game they played in, a junior or college game they keep the book for. Reads rule/sport_ice_hockey for every value. Owns tags: match (with ice_hockey), book-kept, no-book, shootout, three-stars, series. Does not cover fantasy matchups (rule/app_fantasy) or roster moves (rule/rosters_and_staff).

lore.title: Logging a game
lore.content:
1. Find the game: search_entities event with the two teams and the date, and the season's scheduled games for that date. A pro schedule is usually pre-loaded (status scheduled); a rec game usually is not. Create only when nothing matches, named "<Away> at <Home> — <YYYY-MM-DD>", PART_OF the season (or PART_OF the series parent in the playoffs, round "Game N"), HELD_AT the arena, two COMPETED_IN edges, tags ice_hockey, <season tag>, match.
2. Score: home_score and away_score in goals (the shootout winner's extra goal included), decided_by regulation / overtime / shootout / forfeit / run_rule, score_display when not regulation ("4-3 OT", "2-1 SO", "3-2 2OT"), result, and result on both COMPETED_IN edges. Ask one question if the owner says "won in extra time" without saying OT or shootout; a playoff game cannot be a shootout.
3. Period goals, shots and special teams when given: team match stat_lines per side (goals_p1..goals_ot, goals_so, shots_for, pp_goals, pp_opportunities, pim), and the event's periods array ({number, home, away} per period) when the owner wants the line score on the game. Shootout detail (rounds, shooters, who scored) in event lore "Shootout" plus so_attempts/so_goals/so_gdg on skater lines and so_shots_faced/so_saves on goalie lines, when the owner gives them.
4. Who played, only if the competition is tagged lineups-tracked: PLAYED_IN per dressed player, started for the goalie, played false for the backup who sat; the sign-in sheet at rec level. Check the roster edges per rule/recording_a_match (a borrowed goalie is arrangement substitute).
5. Box score: one match stat_line per player with numbers, keys from the pack (skater g a pts plus_minus pim shots hits blocks toi_seconds ppg shg gwg fow fol; goalie gs w l otl ga sa sv so toi_seconds). Convert mm:ss to seconds. Check pts = g + a and sv = sa - ga before saving; ask on a mismatch. completeness full and tag book-kept when the full sheet was entered; completeness partial (or unknown) and tag no-book when only the score or part of the sheet is known. Goalie of record: exactly one goalie per side gets the decision (w, l or otl = 1).
6. Update: the team season lines with source derived (the standings join: result plus decided_by -> w rw / w otw / w sow / l / otl / t, pts by the competition's scoring_system; gf, ga, splits, streak_len, last10; an owner or official line is left alone and flagged), player season lines (sum, games_played, as_of, source derived, "Derived from" lore), the series parent's score_display and status in the playoffs, and season.current_round. Say what changed in one line: "Logged the 4-3 OT win; you're 12-6-3, 27 points, third in the division on regulation wins."
7. Story: lore chunks on the event titled Summary, Key moments (goals with time and assists as the owner gives them, "Lee (Kim, Park) 12:41 2nd PP"), Penalties (time, player, infraction, minutes as the scoresheet lists them), Shootout, Conditions, Notes. Three stars as WON edges with "First Star", "Second Star", "Third Star".

lore.title: Questions people ask the next day
lore.content: "How are we doing": the team season line (W-L-OTL, points, division place if the whole division is on file; otherwise say the table is partial). "Who's hot": last five match lines for the team's skaters, sum g and a, say the span. "Goalie numbers": sv_pct = sv / sa and gaa = ga * 3600 / toi_seconds over the games with a kept book; quote the count. "Record in OT/shootouts": count COMPETED_IN results joined to decided_by. "Next game": get_timeline from today for the team, event_type match, status scheduled. "Who's on IR / out": PLAYS_FOR edges with role injured_reserve or availability unavailable, listed with roster_list, availability_until when set, and the date of the latest roster_move event, never a reason.

lore.title: Health language, once
lore.content: Game-night talk is full of "upper-body", "day-to-day", "left the game and didn't return", "concussion protocol". Record the sporting consequence only: played false or entered_at for the replacement, availability unavailable or doubtful on the roster edge, role injured_reserve with roster_list when the team designates it. If the owner types a medical detail, leave it out, log everything else, and say in one line that this world keeps no health details. Do not argue, do not repeat the warning every game.
